notes: Simple 2-column list, no caption line above the column labels (the header strip holds only the two labels). Column 1 = nominal bar diameter in mm, column 2 = theoretical weight in kg/m, printed with 3 decimals and a dot as decimal separator; trailing zeros kept as printed. 16 rows, no empty cells, no footnotes, no merged cells. The steel grade / standard (B500B, EN 10080) is not printed in these two images. Transcribed exactly as printed (not corrected): the first two rows are printed "0.092" (diameter 4) and "0.144" (diameter 5); both were read pixel-exact, but they differ from the usual nominal masses for these diameters (remark only, not part of the transcription: 0.00617 x d^2 gives about 0.099 and 0.154), so they look like deviations/typos in the source - all other rows look ordinary.
